title: Failed steam traps repaired, with site constants
grade: First draft on site constants: every constant is a site value, but the measured inputs are as entered and have not been checked against a representative period.
assumptions: Failed steam traps on the 150 psig main: the steam rate entered holds for all 8,760 h/yr.
Failed steam traps on the 150 psig main: each pound of steam carries the stated energy from feedwater to steam, and the steam conditions do not change through the year.
Failed steam traps on the 150 psig main: boiler efficiency is constant at this load, and the fuel saved is priced at the margin.
Failed steam traps on the 150 psig main: Scope 1 covers combustion only (no upstream fuel supply); water, treatment chemicals and pumping are not costed.
Where a range is entered, the result carries both ends. That is the spread of what was entered, not a probability interval.
to_firm_up: Confirm by measurement: Steam flow saved or lost, lb/h: a steam flowmeter, or a survey estimate (for failed traps, the survey's orifice-based loss per trap; DOE Steam Tip Sheet #1 prints one such table).
Confirm by measurement: Steam pressure (psig) and temperature at the point of loss, and the feedwater or makeup water temperature: gauges, the historian, the deaerator.
Confirm by measurement: Operating hours per year the change applies: historian run status, the operating schedule, or maintenance records. Not 8,760 unless it really runs all year.
After the change, measure the same quantities again at the same production rate: that before/after pair, not this estimate, is the saving.

fuel_price_per_mmbtu.label: site value: 0.55 $/therm / 0.1 MMBtu/therm (exact unit definition); ILLUSTRATIVE delivered gas price from a made-up gas bill

fuel_kg_co2e_per_mmbtu.label: site value: ILLUSTRATIVE, rounded from the EPA Hub natural gas factor

boiler_efficiency.label: site value: ILLUSTRATIVE range from a made-up boiler test

changes.change: Failed steam traps on the 150 psig main

steam_energy.label: site value: ILLUSTRATIVE steam-table value (steam enthalpy minus feedwater enthalpy)

steps.formula: lb/h x hours x Btu/lb / 1,000,000 Btu/MMBtu

limits: An estimate from the inputs shown, not a measured or verified saving. It is only as good as the measured kW, flow and hours; a before/after measurement at the same production rate is the proof.
Fuel CO2e is Scope 1 combustion only (no upstream). Steam and heat become fuel through the boiler efficiency given; water, treatment chemicals, maintenance and pumping are not costed.
No savings come from a drawing alone: every quantity here was measured or supplied by the user.
